wiki.extract: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a well-preserved fortress on a hill on the island of St. Kitts, in the Federation of St. Christopher and Nevis in the Eastern Caribbean. It was designed by British military engineers, and was built and maintained by enslaved Africans. It is one of the best preserved historical fortifications in the Americas.

Mount Liamuiga is a 1,156-metre (3,792 ft) stratovolcano which forms the north-western part of the island of Saint Kitts. The peak is the highest point on the island of Saint Kitts, in the federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis, and in the entire British Leeward Islands, as well as one of the tallest peaks in the eastern Caribbean archipelago. The peak is topped by a 1-kilometre (0.6 mi) wide summit crater, which contained a shallow crater lake until 1959. As of 2006, the crater lake had re-formed. The last verified eruptions from the volcano were about 1,800 years ago, while reports of possible eruptions in 1692 and 1843 are considered uncertain.
St. Kitts Scenic Railway is a 29-kilometre (18 mi) long narrow-gauge railway line along the coastline of the island of St. Kitts in the eastern Caribbean, with a track gauge of 762 mm.

Romney Manor is a building in the Wingfield Estate in Saint Kitts. Samuel Jefferson bought the estate in 1625 and established a sugar plantation there. It was subsequently named after the Earl of Romney, who bought it from the Jeffersons in 1713. The sugar plantation used slave labour until 1834. Today it is a tourist destination, home to a batik enterprise and a botanical garden.

Nevis Peak is a potentially active volcano which is located in the centre of the island of Nevis of the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis in the West Indies. The stratovolcano rises to a height of 985 metres (3,232 ft) and is the highest point on the island. There have been no eruptions since prehistory, but there are active fumaroles and hot springs on the coastal slopes of the island, and these represent low-level volcanic activity.

cultural_events.name: St. Kitts and Nevis National Carnival (Sugar Mas)

wiki.extract: The  culture of St. Kitts and Nevis, two small Caribbean islands forming one country, has grown mainly out of the West African traditions of the slave population brought in during the colonial period. France and British colonists both settled the islands, and for a period of time the British imported indentured Irish servants. The native Caribs, skilled warriors, defended their lands by attacking the colonies. But by 1782, the British had gained control of St. Kitts and Nevis, which they retained until granting the islands their independence in 1983. British influence remains in the country's official language, English, while some islanders speak an English-based Creole. The influence of the French, Irish, and Carib seems less pronounced.

The St. Kitts Music Festival is a festival of popular music held annually in June on the Caribbean islands of St. Kitts. The festival was originally called the Shak Shak Festival, and was first held in 1996. The first Festival featured Arrow, Nigel Lewis, Roy Cape Band, Krosfyah, Nu Vybes and the Small Axe Band, as well as the Su Wen-Ching Chinese Ensemble.

Each year, Nevisians celebrate their heritage during Culturama. It is Nevis' answer to the diverse range of carnivals enjoyed on other Caribbean islands. Held annually in late July/early August, it celebrates Nevisians who have moved away and returned to party with their friends and family. It is a commemoration and festival enjoying the cultural traditions. There's music every night, parties, food festivals, and concerts, culminating in the early march through downtown Charlestown.

Nevis is an island in the Caribbean Sea that forms part of the inner arc of the Leeward Islands chain of the West Indies. Nevis and the neighbouring island of Saint Kitts constitute the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis, a sovereign state. Nevis is located near the northern end of the Lesser Antilles archipelago about 350 kilometres (220 mi) east-southeast of Puerto Rico and 80 kilometres (50 mi) west of Antigua. Its area is 93 square kilometres (36 sq mi) and the capital is Charlestown.
Saint Mary Cayon is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is located on the main island of Saint Kitts and the parish capital is Cayon.

food_writeup: Kittitian and Nevisian cuisine blends African, British and Creole influences. The national dish is goat water, a hearty stew, alongside saltfish, johnny cakes and fresh seafood like conch and lobster. Sugar cane, once the island's lifeblood, still flavours local sweets and rum.
brief_history: St Kitts was the first English colony in the Caribbean (1623) and, with Nevis, became a wealthy sugar colony built on enslaved African labour. After centuries of plantation rule and the sugar industry's closure in 2005, the federation gained independence from Britain in 1983. A 1998 Nevis secession referendum failed, and the islands now thrive on tourism and financial services.
current_conflicts: Saint Kitts and Nevis has no armed conflict, but gang-related gun violence is a persistent concern for the small federation. The government has also faced international scrutiny over its Citizenship by Investment programme.

main_events.headline: Tourism takes over from sugar

main_events.headline: Debt among the highest in the world
main_events.summary: Public debt tops 130% of GDP, among the highest ratios globally, as the IMF urges fiscal consolidation.

sport.headline: Warner Park readied for the Cricket World Cup
sport.summary: Basseterre's Warner Park is upgraded to host 2007 Cricket World Cup matches, the biggest sporting event in the country's history.

main_events.headline: After sugar: the diversification push
main_events.summary: Two years after the sugar industry's closure, the Douglas government courts tourism and offshore investment to fill the gap.

main_events.headline: Economy grows on construction and tourism
main_events.summary: GDP expands as hotel construction and visitor arrivals climb, though the debt burden stays heavy.

sport.headline: Kim Collins at the Osaka World Championships
sport.summary: Kittitian sprint star Kim Collins competes in the sprints at the World Championships in Osaka.

main_events.headline: Hurricane Omar brushes the islands
main_events.summary: Category 4 Hurricane Omar passes near St Kitts and Nevis in October, causing coastal damage but sparing the islands the worst.

main_events.headline: Global crisis hits tourism
main_events.summary: The financial crisis dents visitor arrivals and CBI applications, squeezing the twin-island economy.

sport.headline: Kim Collins at his fourth Olympics
sport.summary: Collins competes in the 100m and 200m at the Beijing Olympics, his fourth Games.

main_events.headline: Government opens debt talks with creditors
main_events.summary: With debt above 120% of GDP, Basseterre begins restructuring talks with the IMF and Paris Club creditors.

main_events.headline: Tourism slump deepens the downturn
main_events.summary: Visitor arrivals fall sharply in the global recession and the economy contracts.

sport.headline: Kim Collins runs at the Berlin World Championships
sport.summary: Collins represents St Kitts and Nevis in the sprints at the World Championships in Berlin.

main_events.headline: Denzil Douglas wins a fifth term
main_events.summary: Douglas's Labour Party narrowly wins the January general election, extending his 15-year rule.

main_events.headline: VAT introduced to fix the finances
main_events.summary: A 17% value-added tax takes effect in November as part of an IMF-backed fiscal repair programme.

sport.headline: Kittitian athletes at the Delhi Commonwealth Games
sport.summary: St Kitts and Nevis sends a small team to the Commonwealth Games in New Delhi.

main_events.headline: Landmark debt-for-land swap
main_events.summary: Creditors agree to swap debt for government land in a pioneering deal that sharply cuts the debt ratio.

main_events.headline: Debt ratio falls dramatically
main_events.summary: The swap and fiscal tightening bring public debt down from about 135% toward 118% of GDP.

sport.headline: Kim Collins wins World bronze at 35
sport.summary: Collins storms to 100m bronze at the World Championships in Daegu, defying his age.

main_events.headline: Opposition files no-confidence motion
main_events.summary: The opposition tables a no-confidence motion against Douglas in December; it is never debated.

main_events.summary: Senior ministers clash with Douglas as political tensions rise within the government.

sport.summary: Team officials expel Collins from the London Olympics after he visits his wife at a hotel, sparking an international row.

main_events.summary: Timothy Harris is fired from cabinet in January and later launches the Team Unity opposition alliance.

main_events.headline: No-confidence motion gathers dust

sport.summary: St Kitts and Nevis fields sprinters at the World Championships in Moscow.

main_events.headline: Political deadlock drags on
main_events.summary: The Douglas government survives another year without facing the no-confidence motion.

main_events.headline: Economy stabilizes after debt deal
main_events.summary: Growth resumes modestly as the debt restructuring beds in and tourism recovers.

sport.headline: Kim Collins wins Commonwealth bronze

main_events.headline: Team Unity ends Douglas's 20-year rule
main_events.summary: Timothy Harris's Team Unity coalition wins the February election, ousting Douglas after two decades in power.
